candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days' — the closing inclusio of the entire Mäṣḥafä Hēnok. The book closes as it opens (cf. 1En 1:1-2): with Enoch writing for the future-righteous-remnant. Tewahedo manuscript-tradition preserves this opening-closing inclusio as the book's own self-attestation to its destination: it is FOR THE LAST-DAYS RIGHTEOUS. The Tewahedo identification with this addressee is preserved in the very fact that the Tewahedo Bible is the ONLY canonical Bible in which 1 Enoch closes: that closing-charge IS to the Tewahedo reader.
